evidence.title: Hybrid Solar and Kinetic Energy Harvesting System for Smart Microgrids for EV Charging With Integrated IOT
evidence.abstract: This project presents a Hybrid Solar and Kinetic Energy Harvesting System designed for efficient energy harvesting and smart microgrid management. The system integrates a 12V battery, charged via a photovoltaic (PV) cell and an energy harvesting mechanism from a speed breaker, ensuring a sustainable power supply. One 1W solar panel, each monitored by a voltage sensor, provide real-time voltage data to an Arduino UNO microcontroller. Simultaneously, the speed breaker-based energy harvester contributes additional power, monitored through a voltage sensor. To enhance system intelligence and remote accessibility, an IoT-enabled Wi-Fi module transmits real-time power data to an online monitoring platform. The system optimizes power distribution across three load stations using relay-based control, allowing dynamic load management based on power availability and demand. By integrating solar and kinetic energy sources, this project enhances energy efficiency and reliability in smart microgrid applications.

evidence.title: The Case for Modeling Security, Privacy, Usability and Reliability (SPUR) in Automotive Software
evidence.abstract: Over the past five years, there has been considerable growth and established value in the practice of modeling automotive software requirements. Much of this growth has been centered on requirements of software associated with the established functional areas of an automobile, such as those associated with powertrain, chassis, body, safety and infotainment. This paper makes a case for modeling four additional attributes that are increasingly important as vehicles become information conduits: security, privacy, usability, and reliability. These four attributes are important in creating specifications for embedded in-vehicle automotive software.

evidence.title: Towards a Systems Engineering based Automotive Product Engineering Process
evidence.abstract: Deficit and redundancies in existing automotive product development hinder a systems engineering based development. In this paper we discuss a methodical procedure to eliminate deficits in the current product development and in turn to enable the introduction of a new systems engineering based development methodology. As the core part of our approach, we discuss how to transform an opaque heterogeneous product development to a homogenous consistent product development taking into account existing disciplines. Our approach paves the way to achieve a process structure that is more amenable to verification and validation. We show the effectiveness of our proposed solution approach on an automotive use case.

evidence.title: Design, Construction and Evaluation of a Power-Dense 12 V to 48 V Bidirectional DC-DC converter for Automotive Applications
evidence.abstract: Power dense and highly efficient converters are becoming very important in the electric vehicle industry. They have the capability of reducing the power consumption of an electric vehicle by reducing the overall weight of the vehicle. This dissertation report introduces a 1.5kW power dense and highly efficient DC-DC bidirectional converter (12V to 48V). Planar magnetics, thermally conducting substrate, and double-sided cooling semiconductor devices were used to design this converter. Interphase transformer based dual interleaved boost topology was chosen for the converter. A full bridge configuration was selected to ensure bidirectional power flow in the circuit. Semiconductor devices, magnetic cores, capacitors, heat sink, and connectors were selected based on the electrical, mechanical, and thermal optimization of each component. The power circuit layout was done on a thermal clad board in a careful manner to ensure symmetry and low parasitic impedance. After testing the converter, the results were analysed based on the steady state and dynamic operation of an interphase transformer based dual interleaved boost converter. All the waveforms were found to be in close proximity with the theory and specifications. The planar interphase transformer showed a high coupling and good current sharing between its windings. The power loss and temperature of different components were found closely matched with design predictions. An efficiency of around 94% was found in both boost and buck mode of operation at the rated condition. With the heat sink and without the heat sink, the power densities were found 1.8 kW/litre and 5.1 kW/litre, respectively. The designed converter showed that a high efficiency and a high power density can be achieved with off-the-shelf components. This converter can be used in an electric vehicle to interface auxiliary loads with the 12V battery. It can also be used in an aircraft or in an electric ship for the same purpose.

evidence.title: Modeling and Control of a 7-phase Claw-pole Starter-alternator for a Micro-hybrid Automotive Application
evidence.abstract: This paper deals with the modeling and the control of a new high power 12V Integrated Starter Alternator (ISA). This system is used to bring micro-hybrid functions to standard Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles. The drive is composed of a seven-phase synchronous claw-pole machine with separate excitation, supplied with a seven-leg Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) designed for low voltage and high current. The system is modeled in a generalized Concordia frame and a graphical description is used to highlight energetic properties of such a complex system. A control scheme is then deduced from this graphical description. Two controls are achieved in generator mode and compared: one is using the VSI in a square-wave mode, the other in a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) mode. Experimental results are provided.This work was supported by the French car supplier Valeoand the regional council of France Region-Nord-Pas-De-Calais

evidence.title: Computational and experimental study of air hybrid engine concepts
evidence.abstract: The air hybrid engine absorbs the vehicle kinetic energy during braking, stores it in an air tank in the form of compressed air, and reuses it to start the engine and to propel a vehicle during cruising and acceleration.Capturing, storing and reusing this braking energy to achieve stop-start operation and to give additional power can therefore improve fuel economy, particularly in cities and urban areas where the traffic conditions involve many stops and starts.In order to reuse the residual kinetic energy, the vehicle operation consists of 3 basic modes, i.e.Compression Mode (CM), Expander Mode (EM) and normal firing mode, as well as stop-start operation through an air starter.A four-cylinder 2 litre diesel engine has been modelled to operate in four air hybrid engine configurations so that the braking and motoring performance of each configuration could be studied.These air hybrid systems can be constructed with production technologies and incur minimum changes to the existing engine design.The regenerative engine braking and starting capability is realised through the employment of an innovative simple one-way intake system and a production cam profile switching (CPS) mechanism.The hybrid systems will allow the engine to be cranked by the compressed air at moderate pressure without using addition starters or dedicated valves in the cylinder head.Therefore, the proposed air hybrid engine systems can be considered as a cost-effective regenerative hybrid powertrain and can be implemented in vehicles using existing production technologies.

evidence.title: Design of a switched reluctance machine drive for automotive applications
evidence.abstract: Automotive electrical systems are currently 12Vdc supplied from an engine driven alternator.In an effort to meet electrical system demands of the future this voltage will be increased to a 42Vdc standard.Operating at this increased voltage level will facilitate numerous electronic systems to be incorporated into the vehicle in order to improve safety, increase fuel efficiency and reduce emissions.As part of the initiative the starter and alternator will be integrated into a single unit.The 42-volt bus will allow for a more powerful integrated starter alternator (ISA).The switched reluctance motor (SRM) could be considered as a viable solution for implementing integrated starter alternator.The SRM is a low maintenance, low cost, rugged, brushless motor without permanent magnets.It has a rugged construction that is ideally suited for automotive applications with its harsh under-bonnet environment.It provides high torque and power relative to motor volume.The principal disadvantages of this type of motor include the motor design and control difficulties Modern motor design software and lower cost digital signal processing chips for motor control have overcome these difficulties.This thesis discusses the automotive electrical systems, switched reluctance motors (SRM), converter configurations.The operation and the design of a 3.5kW full bridge converter and its associated control circuitry to facilitate the SRM to operate in starter and alternator modes are described in detail.I would like to thank PEI Technologies and DCU for financial support and assistance during the course of this research.

mechanism_map.mechanism: A 12V battery is kept charged by an auxiliary renewable harvester (photovoltaic cell plus kinetic energy harvester) with voltage-sensor monitoring and relay-based load management, ensuring a sustainable power supply and dynamic load management based on power availability and demand.
mechanism_map.intervention: Install a low-wattage PV trickle charger (and/or a small kinetic/vibration harvester) on the vehicle's 12V starter battery, interposed by a charge controller with a voltage sensor and a relay that priority-switches or disconnects non-essential parasitic loads when the battery voltage falls below a threshold, so the battery is replenished and protected during idle periods without manual terminal disconnect.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: The harvested trickle charge offsets the standing parasitic drain, holding the battery above the no-start threshold so full cranking power remains available after at least one week idle.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Baseline-test a vehicle battery's resting voltage and cold-cranking amps, then leave the vehicle idle for 7 days with the parasitic load active; repeat with the PV trickle-charge/relay controller fitted and log battery voltage every hour. The mechanism is falsified if the 7-day voltage under the intervention does not stay above ~12.4 V (or fails to deliver rated CCA and a start), or if the relay fails to shed the parasitic load when voltage drops below the set threshold.
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: The system integrates a 12V battery, charged via a photovoltaic (PV) cell and an energy harvesting mechanism from a speed breaker, ensuring a sustainable power supply.

candidates.mechanism: A linear pass-element power stage holds the cranking-bus voltage at a fixed setpoint by operating in its linear region and dissipating the excess of battery terminal voltage as heat, decoupling the starter-bus voltage from the terminal-voltage decay produced by parasitic drain.
candidates.intervention: Insert a linear voltage-stabilization power-electronic module in the 12V starter battery's output feed (battery to starter/cranking bus) that regulates the cranking bus to a fixed setpoint instead of feeding the starter directly from the bare terminals.

candidates.mechanism: A 12V starter battery is replenished while parked only by a parking-operant source (low-wattage photovoltaic panel, dash-/parcel-shelf-mounted, indoors or outdoors), and its remaining charge is defended by a low-voltage-disconnect (LVD) relay that isolates non-essential parasitic loads once the battery sags toward a calibrated reserve floor. The kinetic/speed-breaker harvester is removed from the energy budget entirely, so no part of the charge budget depends on vehicle motion.
candidates.intervention: Fit a ~5-15 W PV panel with a charge controller and voltage sensor across the 12V battery, and interpose an LVD relay on the non-essential load bus (infotainment, telematics, keyless-entry/comfort bus) set to open at ~12.2-12.3 V and reclose only above ~12.6 V; no kinetic harvester, no speed-breaker component, no manual terminal disconnect.
candidates.predicted_effect: After 7 days parked with the parasitic load active, the battery stays at or above ~12.4 V and delivers rated cold-cranking amps and a normal start; if harvest is insufficient (e.g., dark parking), the LVD isolates the parasitic load and still preserves a starting reserve of at least ~12.2 V.
candidates.testable_prediction: Measure the vehicle's standing parasitic drain and resting voltage/CCA; log battery voltage hourly over a 7-day idle with the parasitic load active, first baseline, then with the PV+LVD module fitted (repeat in both a lit and a dark/garaged parking condition). The mechanism is falsified if the 7-day voltage under intervention falls below ~12.4 V in the lit case, below ~12.2 V with the LVD having disconnected loads in the dark case, or if the unit fails to deliver rated CCA and a start at the end of either run.
candidates.mechanism_source_span: The system integrates a 12V battery, charged via a photovoltaic (PV) cell and an energy harvesting mechanism from a speed breaker, ensuring a sustainable power supply.
candidates.support_state_note: IMPROVE_CHILD_SUPPORT_NOT_ADJUDICATED: the child's mutated mechanism has no mechanism-space evidence adjudication; the release gate holds non-affirmative support states (R401 Phase 4)

kill_basis.verdict: KILLED - the cited source provides a 1 W solar panel plus a speed-breaker kinetic harvester, but a speed breaker (a road hump) is stationary when the vehicle is parked, so the kinetic harvester contributes zero power during the one-week idle that the constraint specifies; the record's own mechanism_source_span names "speed breaker-based energy harvester" which cannot operate while the car is idle, so the trickle-charge budget that must offset the parasitic drain is not produced by the record's own mechanism.

derivation_trace.causal_change: The parent's charge budget included a speed-breaker kinetic harvester that produces exactly zero power while the vehicle is parked (the kill mechanism); the child deletes that harvester and makes the budget depend solely on a parking-operant PV panel, with the LVD relay guaranteeing starting reserve when harvest is zero — so the mechanism's stated energy source can actually exist during the specified one-week idle.
derivation_trace.novel_design_variable: The low-voltage-disconnect threshold and hysteresis on the non-essential load bus (open ~12.2-12.3 V, reclose ~12.6 V), which decouples "reliably starts after extended parking" from "harvest must always exceed parasitic drain."

attacks.weak_transfer: RISK - the source application is a stationary smart-microgrid EV-charging kiosk continuously exposed to solar irradiance and active vehicle traffic over a speed breaker, whereas the target is a parked 12V automotive starter battery indoors or in shade for 7 days; the specific element (continuous kinetic excitation from passing traffic) is the one that fails to transfer, and the record's own 1 W solar nameplate versus a typical 50–100 mA automotive parasitic drain (~0.6–1.2 W continuous) leaves the harvested margin not proven to be sufficient, so the kill depends on an operating-point assumption the record never quantifies.

A combination qualifies only if it produces a demonstrably new technical effect that survives prior art and non-obviousness attack. A world-class invention needs a genuinely new technical information source, transformation, or control capability. Do not build an AI layer on top of an already-claimed sensing/control architecture.' Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.

A query-fragile search produces false negatives.' The machine must be better at discovering what competitors actually claimed than it is at inventing elegant names for what we hope is new.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Stroke Round 58; applies to all latent-variable inventions)
warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.lesson: ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages mask catastrophic failure modes. Thermal activation in a 37°C body environment has a narrow window (37-45°C = 8°C max). Sensor electronics are a SPOF that cannot be fully resolved by redundancy (common-mode failures).

informational.lesson: Do not assume VP shunt problems apply to the eShunt. The eShunt's drainage geometry is fundamentally different (short path, no siphon). Always verify the problem exists for the SPECIFIC device geometry. Over-drainage is siphon-driven; without a hydrostatic column, it may not occur.

informational.mechanism: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: This project presents a Hybrid Solar and Kinetic Energy Harvesting System designed for efficient energy harvesting and smart microgrid management. The system integrates a 12V battery, charged via a photovoltaic (PV) cell and an energy harvesting mechanism from a speed breaker, ensuring a sustainable power supply. One 1W solar panel, each monitored by a voltage sensor, provide real-time voltage data to an Arduino UNO microcontroller. Simultaneously, the speed breaker-based energy harvester contributes additional power, monitored through a voltage sensor. To enhance system intelligence and remote accessibility, an IoT-enabled Wi-Fi module transmits real-time power data to an online monitoring platform. The system optimizes power distribution across three load stations using relay-based control, allowing dynamic load management based on power availability and demand. By integrating solar and kinetic energy sources, this project enhances energy efficiency and reliability in smart microgrid applications.

custody_records.raw_content: Over the past five years, there has been considerable growth and established value in the practice of modeling automotive software requirements. Much of this growth has been centered on requirements of software associated with the established functional areas of an automobile, such as those associated with powertrain, chassis, body, safety and infotainment. This paper makes a case for modeling four additional attributes that are increasingly important as vehicles become information conduits: security, privacy, usability, and reliability. These four attributes are important in creating specifications for embedded in-vehicle automotive software.

custody_records.raw_content: Deficit and redundancies in existing automotive product development hinder a systems engineering based development. In this paper we discuss a methodical procedure to eliminate deficits in the current product development and in turn to enable the introduction of a new systems engineering based development methodology. As the core part of our approach, we discuss how to transform an opaque heterogeneous product development to a homogenous consistent product development taking into account existing disciplines. Our approach paves the way to achieve a process structure that is more amenable to verification and validation. We show the effectiveness of our proposed solution approach on an automotive use case.

custody_records.raw_content: This work aims to connect the Automotive User Interfaces (Auto-UI) and Conversational User Interfaces (CUI) communities through discussion of their shared view of the future of automotive conversational user interfaces. The workshop aims to encourage creative consideration of optimistic and pessimistic futures, encouraging attendees to explore the opportunities and barriers that lie ahead through a game. Considerations of the future will be mapped out in greater detail through the drafting of research agendas, by which attendees will get to know each other's expertise and networks of resources. The two day workshop, consisting of two 90-minute sessions, will facilitate greater communication and collaboration between these communities, connecting researchers to work together to influence the futures they imagine in the workshop.

custody_records.raw_content: Power dense and highly efficient converters are becoming very important in the electric vehicle industry. They have the capability of reducing the power consumption of an electric vehicle by reducing the overall weight of the vehicle. This dissertation report introduces a 1.5kW power dense and highly efficient DC-DC bidirectional converter (12V to 48V). Planar magnetics, thermally conducting substrate, and double-sided cooling semiconductor devices were used to design this converter. Interphase transformer based dual interleaved boost topology was chosen for the converter. A full bridge configuration was selected to ensure bidirectional power flow in the circuit. Semiconductor devices, magnetic cores, capacitors, heat sink, and connectors were selected based on the electrical, mechanical, and thermal optimization of each component. The power circuit layout was done on a thermal clad board in a careful manner to ensure symmetry and low parasitic impedance. After testing the converter, the results were analysed based on the steady state and dynamic operation of an interphase transformer based dual interleaved boost converter. All the waveforms were found to be in close proximity with the theory and specifications. The planar interphase transformer showed a high coupling and good current sharing between its windings. The power loss and temperature of different components were found closely matched with design predictions. An efficiency of around 94% was found in both boost and buck mode of operation at the rated condition. With the heat sink and without the heat sink, the power densities were found 1.8 kW/litre and 5.1 kW/litre, respectively. The designed converter showed that a high efficiency and a high power density can be achieved with off-the-shelf components. This converter can be used in an electric vehicle to interface auxiliary loads with the 12V battery. It can also be used in an aircraft or in an electric ship for the same purpose.

custody_records.raw_content: This paper deals with the modeling and the control of a new high power 12V Integrated Starter Alternator (ISA). This system is used to bring micro-hybrid functions to standard Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles. The drive is composed of a seven-phase synchronous claw-pole machine with separate excitation, supplied with a seven-leg Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) designed for low voltage and high current. The system is modeled in a generalized Concordia frame and a graphical description is used to highlight energetic properties of such a complex system. A control scheme is then deduced from this graphical description. Two controls are achieved in generator mode and compared: one is using the VSI in a square-wave mode, the other in a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) mode. Experimental results are provided.This work was supported by the French car supplier Valeoand the regional council of France Region-Nord-Pas-De-Calais

custody_records.raw_content: The air hybrid engine absorbs the vehicle kinetic energy during braking, stores it in an air tank in the form of compressed air, and reuses it to start the engine and to propel a vehicle during cruising and acceleration.Capturing, storing and reusing this braking energy to achieve stop-start operation and to give additional power can therefore improve fuel economy, particularly in cities and urban areas where the traffic conditions involve many stops and starts.In order to reuse the residual kinetic energy, the vehicle operation consists of 3 basic modes, i.e.Compression Mode (CM), Expander Mode (EM) and normal firing mode, as well as stop-start operation through an air starter.A four-cylinder 2 litre diesel engine has been modelled to operate in four air hybrid engine configurations so that the braking and motoring performance of each configuration could be studied.These air hybrid systems can be constructed with production technologies and incur minimum changes to the existing engine design.The regenerative engine braking and starting capability is realised through the employment of an innovative simple one-way intake system and a production cam profile switching (CPS) mechanism.The hybrid systems will allow the engine to be cranked by the compressed air at moderate pressure without using addition starters or dedicated valves in the cylinder head.Therefore, the proposed air hybrid engine systems can be considered as a cost-effective regenerative hybrid powertrain and can be implemented in vehicles using existing production technologies.

doi:10.5281/zenodo.21549560.title: Hybrid Solar and Kinetic Energy Harvesting System for Smart Microgrids for EV Charging With Integrated IOT
doi:10.5281/zenodo.21549560.abstract: This project presents a Hybrid Solar and Kinetic Energy Harvesting System designed for efficient energy harvesting and smart microgrid management. The system integrates a 12V battery, charged via a photovoltaic (PV) cell and an energy harvesting mechanism from a speed breaker, ensuring a sustainable power supply. One 1W solar panel, each monitored by a voltage sensor, provide real-time voltage data to an Arduino UNO microcontroller. Simultaneously, the speed breaker-based energy harvester contributes additional power, monitored through a voltage sensor. To enhance system intelligence and remote accessibility, an IoT-enabled Wi-Fi module transmits real-time power data to an online monitoring platform. The system optimizes power distribution across three load stations using relay-based control, allowing dynamic load management based on power availability and demand. By integrating solar and kinetic energy sources, this project enhances energy efficiency and reliability in smart microgrid applications.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.0604019.title: The Case for Modeling Security, Privacy, Usability and Reliability (SPUR) in Automotive Software
doi:10.48550/arxiv.0604019.abstract: Over the past five years, there has been considerable growth and established value in the practice of modeling automotive software requirements. Much of this growth has been centered on requirements of software associated with the established functional areas of an automobile, such as those associated with powertrain, chassis, body, safety and infotainment. This paper makes a case for modeling four additional attributes that are increasingly important as vehicles become information conduits: security, privacy, usability, and reliability. These four attributes are important in creating specifications for embedded in-vehicle automotive software.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.2007.11897.title: Towards a Systems Engineering based Automotive Product Engineering Process
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2007.11897.abstract: Deficit and redundancies in existing automotive product development hinder a systems engineering based development. In this paper we discuss a methodical procedure to eliminate deficits in the current product development and in turn to enable the introduction of a new systems engineering based development methodology. As the core part of our approach, we discuss how to transform an opaque heterogeneous product development to a homogenous consistent product development taking into account existing disciplines. Our approach paves the way to achieve a process structure that is more amenable to verification and validation. We show the effectiveness of our proposed solution approach on an automotive use case.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.2110.10285.abstract: This work aims to connect the Automotive User Interfaces (Auto-UI) and Conversational User Interfaces (CUI) communities through discussion of their shared view of the future of automotive conversational user interfaces. The workshop aims to encourage creative consideration of optimistic and pessimistic futures, encouraging attendees to explore the opportunities and barriers that lie ahead through a game. Considerations of the future will be mapped out in greater detail through the drafting of research agendas, by which attendees will get to know each other's expertise and networks of resources. The two day workshop, consisting of two 90-minute sessions, will facilitate greater communication and collaboration between these communities, connecting researchers to work together to influence the futures they imagine in the workshop.

title:3462ede5879a797c.title: Design, Construction and Evaluation of a Power-Dense 12 V to 48 V Bidirectional DC-DC converter for Automotive Applications
title:3462ede5879a797c.abstract: Power dense and highly efficient converters are becoming very important in the electric vehicle industry. They have the capability of reducing the power consumption of an electric vehicle by reducing the overall weight of the vehicle. This dissertation report introduces a 1.5kW power dense and highly efficient DC-DC bidirectional converter (12V to 48V). Planar magnetics, thermally conducting substrate, and double-sided cooling semiconductor devices were used to design this converter. Interphase transformer based dual interleaved boost topology was chosen for the converter. A full bridge configuration was selected to ensure bidirectional power flow in the circuit. Semiconductor devices, magnetic cores, capacitors, heat sink, and connectors were selected based on the electrical, mechanical, and thermal optimization of each component. The power circuit layout was done on a thermal clad board in a careful manner to ensure symmetry and low parasitic impedance. After testing the converter, the results were analysed based on the steady state and dynamic operation of an interphase transformer based dual interleaved boost converter. All the waveforms were found to be in close proximity with the theory and specifications. The planar interphase transformer showed a high coupling and good current sharing between its windings. The power loss and temperature of different components were found closely matched with design predictions. An efficiency of around 94% was found in both boost and buck mode of operation at the rated condition. With the heat sink and without the heat sink, the power densities were found 1.8 kW/litre and 5.1 kW/litre, respectively. The designed converter showed that a high efficiency and a high power density can be achieved with off-the-shelf components. This converter can be used in an electric vehicle to interface auxiliary loads with the 12V battery. It can also be used in an aircraft or in an electric ship for the same purpose.

doi:10.1109/vppc.2008.4677668.title: Modeling and Control of a 7-phase Claw-pole Starter-alternator for a Micro-hybrid Automotive Application
doi:10.1109/vppc.2008.4677668.abstract: This paper deals with the modeling and the control of a new high power 12V Integrated Starter Alternator (ISA). This system is used to bring micro-hybrid functions to standard Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles. The drive is composed of a seven-phase synchronous claw-pole machine with separate excitation, supplied with a seven-leg Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) designed for low voltage and high current. The system is modeled in a generalized Concordia frame and a graphical description is used to highlight energetic properties of such a complex system. A control scheme is then deduced from this graphical description. Two controls are achieved in generator mode and compared: one is using the VSI in a square-wave mode, the other in a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) mode. Experimental results are provided.This work was supported by the French car supplier Valeoand the regional council of France Region-Nord-Pas-De-Calais

title:9f2fd9c5dcdcd0a1.title: Computational and experimental study of air hybrid engine concepts
title:9f2fd9c5dcdcd0a1.abstract: The air hybrid engine absorbs the vehicle kinetic energy during braking, stores it in an air tank in the form of compressed air, and reuses it to start the engine and to propel a vehicle during cruising and acceleration.Capturing, storing and reusing this braking energy to achieve stop-start operation and to give additional power can therefore improve fuel economy, particularly in cities and urban areas where the traffic conditions involve many stops and starts.In order to reuse the residual kinetic energy, the vehicle operation consists of 3 basic modes, i.e.Compression Mode (CM), Expander Mode (EM) and normal firing mode, as well as stop-start operation through an air starter.A four-cylinder 2 litre diesel engine has been modelled to operate in four air hybrid engine configurations so that the braking and motoring performance of each configuration could be studied.These air hybrid systems can be constructed with production technologies and incur minimum changes to the existing engine design.The regenerative engine braking and starting capability is realised through the employment of an innovative simple one-way intake system and a production cam profile switching (CPS) mechanism.The hybrid systems will allow the engine to be cranked by the compressed air at moderate pressure without using addition starters or dedicated valves in the cylinder head.Therefore, the proposed air hybrid engine systems can be considered as a cost-effective regenerative hybrid powertrain and can be implemented in vehicles using existing production technologies.

title:f099bf36293961b5.title: Design of a switched reluctance machine drive for automotive applications
title:f099bf36293961b5.abstract: Automotive electrical systems are currently 12Vdc supplied from an engine driven alternator.In an effort to meet electrical system demands of the future this voltage will be increased to a 42Vdc standard.Operating at this increased voltage level will facilitate numerous electronic systems to be incorporated into the vehicle in order to improve safety, increase fuel efficiency and reduce emissions.As part of the initiative the starter and alternator will be integrated into a single unit.The 42-volt bus will allow for a more powerful integrated starter alternator (ISA).The switched reluctance motor (SRM) could be considered as a viable solution for implementing integrated starter alternator.The SRM is a low maintenance, low cost, rugged, brushless motor without permanent magnets.It has a rugged construction that is ideally suited for automotive applications with its harsh under-bonnet environment.It provides high torque and power relative to motor volume.The principal disadvantages of this type of motor include the motor design and control difficulties Modern motor design software and lower cost digital signal processing chips for motor control have overcome these difficulties.This thesis discusses the automotive electrical systems, switched reluctance motors (SRM), converter configurations.The operation and the design of a 3.5kW full bridge converter and its associated control circuitry to facilitate the SRM to operate in starter and alternator modes are described in detail.I would like to thank PEI Technologies and DCU for financial support and assistance during the course of this research.

design_inputs.value: solution must retain enough cranking power to start the engine after at least one week idle without manual terminal disconnect

A 12V starter battery is replenished while parked only by a parking-operant source (low-wattage photovoltaic panel, dash-/parcel-shelf-mounted, indoors or outdoors), and its remaining charge is defended by a low-voltage-disconnect (LVD) relay that isolates non-essential parasitic loads once the battery sags toward a calibrated reserve floor. The kinetic/speed-breaker harvester is removed from the energy budget entirely, so no part of the charge budget depends on vehicle motion.

proposed_design.input: solution must retain enough cranking power to start the engine after at least one week idle without manual terminal disconnect
proposed_design.mechanism: A 12V starter battery is replenished while parked only by a parking-operant source (low-wattage photovoltaic panel, dash-/parcel-shelf-mounted, indoors or outdoors), and its remaining charge is defended by a low-voltage-disconnect (LVD) relay that isolates non-essential parasitic loads once the battery sags toward a calibrated reserve floor. The kinetic/speed-breaker harvester is removed from the energy budget entirely, so no part of the charge budget depends on vehicle motion.

With the heat sink and without the heat sink, the power densities were found 1.8 kW/litre and 5.1 kW/litre, respectively. The designed converter showed that a high efficiency and a high power density can be achieved with off-the-shelf components.
